title: Effects of frame initialization
statement: Let $Z$ be compiler size data with word size $W$, stack capacity $Q$, and frame size $F$, and let $n,q',F'$ be natural numbers and $m$ an initial memory. Suppose the new-frame pointer contains the stack address for $q'$, each pool cell indexed by $2i$ contains the integer $2i$ for every $i<F'$, and $q'+F'\le Q$. After executing the frame-initialization instructions, each stack cell indexed by $q'+i$, for $i<F'$, contains the initial value of temporary cell $i$ if $i<n$, and otherwise the initial value of the zero cell; moreover, memory agrees with its initial value outside the address scratch cell and the stack cells indexed from $q'$ through $Q-1$.
